newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest hydropower dams readied for floods.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest hydropower dams readied for floods.

text.p: Hydroelectric dams in the Pacific Northwest have been readied in the event of possible flooding after the heavy snow and rain which hit much of the region over the last few days, the U.S Army Corps of Engineers said Monday.
"The primary impact so far has been on the Willamette (river)" said Cindy Henriksen, chief of the agency's reservoir control center in Portland, Oregon.

The Corps of Engineers operates most of the federal hydroelectric projects in the Northwest region, the bulk of which are on the Columbia and Snake Rivers rather than the smaller Willamette in western Oregon.

Henriksen noted that reservoir water levels at John Day project were drawn down by increasing outflows in case a new rainstorm melts snowpack along the Snake River, sending more water into the dam system.
In addition, flows through the Grand Coulee dam in Washington state are being kept at daily minimum levels "so we don't get too much outflow," Henriksen said.
She also noted that melting ice and snow in the Columbia Gorge, east of Portland, Ore., could affect operations of the Bonneville Dam, the last project on the Columbia River.
